answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a unique computational thread: before an identity earns trust, it must solve a sequential puzzle seeded by its own public key, a cost that cannot be shared or parallelized across clones. A sybil farmer planting a hundred fake raven identities must pay the full compute price for every single one, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then grows only from verified work done after that proof, so an oasis of fake accounts stays barren - cheap to spawn, too expensive to make useful.
